playbook:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell with a simple randomizing rule biased away from any cluster: rotate among three nonadjacent cells rather than always the center. I will change the trio if opponents pattern around my current trio or if repeated hits show one of my trio is being targeted.

If an opponent repeatedly targets me, I move unpredictably among my three chosen cells (and expand or shift the trio if needed) rather than staying central or repeating the same cell.

When choosing a hiding cell after observing prior hides, I favor cells that opponents have not recently targeted to reduce hit probability. If I see a clear modal for an opponent, I assume they will aim there next and avoid adjacent cells.

When firing I comply with standing-order target identity, but I choose my fired cell using target hide-frequency data: pick the modal cell for that target if a modal exists and the expected payoff justifies the risk; otherwise randomize among three nonadjacent cells to avoid creating a pattern opponents can exploit.

When I have very limited information about a target’s hide tendencies, I randomize my fired cell across three nonadjacent cells to avoid giving opponents an easy pattern to exploit.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I report it exactly as given — I do not lie. I use the true-miss/hit reports to update my model of opponents’ hide distributions and to flag inconsistent public claims from others.

When Harbor is a legal target, I only fire at Harbor if the immediate point transfer and strategic benefit outweigh the political cost and likely reprisal; avoid shooting Harbor purely for spite or predictability unless I consciously decide to become the aggressor.

When arranging escorts, I do not offer blanket mutual escort to multiple players. I offer or accept mutual escort only with a single player who has reliably reciprocated or whose cooperation materially increases my expected points. I will decline escort if no reliable reciprocal partner exists or if accepting would likely fuel an existing alliance that already leads the game.

When posting a public station note, I use concise, actionable signals: report observed targeting patterns, state my intended hiding rotation, or announce willingness to form a specific escort pact. I avoid vague or overly broad mutual-escort language that can be co-opted by two-player alliances.

When I notice opponents mirroring each other or repeatedly supporting one another, I treat them as a probable alliance. I do not mirror them; instead I probe by deviating in low-cost ways (a hide change, a one-off escort offer to a chosen partner, or a single vote deviation) to detect whether the alliance is exploitable or needs to be opposed.

When votes, nominations, or other public actions are required, I watch for consistent pairings and act to exploit or break that alliance depending on my score situation. If two players repeatedly back each other (particularly Foxtrot+Gamma style behavior), I deprioritize giving them free points via escorts and instead look for ways to compete with or destabilize them.

When my score is low relative to others, I prioritize creating opportunities for mutual escorts or targeting the leader with the highest probability-of-hit (based on observed hides) rather than continuing passive mirroring. If a single player is pulling well ahead through repeated successful play or reciprocated escorts, I focus my efforts on reducing their margin (either by accurate shots, arranging counter-escorts that siphon points, or forming ad-hoc coalitions).

When a shot at me is successful, I log the shooter’s last known target cell and increase the probability of shifting away from that cell on my next hide. I also flag repeat shooters as potential threats and adjust my hide trio or rotation speed accordingly.

When public validation of coordinates and claims occurs, I use that transparency to call out inconsistencies promptly. I track every player’s claimed shot results against what I know and what others report; repeated inconsistencies inform distrust and refusal to form pacts.

If an action pattern clearly did not work in prior play (for example, sustained multi-party mutual-escort language that produced no gains and made me predictable), I stop that pattern and adopt probing deviations to gather information and seize scoring chances.

I will prefer offering an escort to a specific single player who has shown clear reciprocity (or who I can credibly expect to reciprocate), rather than public multi-party promises. If I publicly propose an escort, I name the partner explicitly and condition the offer on explicit reciprocation in the next round.

I will track and explicitly record which players consistently target which hides and which players consistently escort each other. I will use that log to inform where I fire, who I offer escorts to, and whether to prioritize disrupting a strong alliance.

I will avoid language that implicitly empowers a two-player coalition (e.g., “mutual with Foxtrot & Gamma”) unless I intend to join them; instead I will state my intentions narrowly and include a clear condition for suspension if not reciprocated.

I will escalate from passive tactics to direct competition when the leader’s point lead is large: prefer firing at the leader when I have a reasonably high chance to hit (based on observed modal hides), and prioritize forming reciprocal escorts with others who can reduce the leader’s advantage.

I will revise my hiding-trio selection periodically (every few rounds or after a hit on me) to remain unpredictable; I will not remain fixed to one labeled trio if it is being read by opponents.

I will use honest claims as a tool: truthful hit/miss reporting keeps my credibility high and allows me to call out others’ inconsistencies; credibility is valuable when negotiating one-on-one escorts or attempting to break alliances.

I will not gift 5 points to form an escort unless the expected long-term return (reciprocity, destabilizing an opponent, or buying an ally) exceeds the immediate cost of enabling an opponent. If there is reasonable doubt about reciprocity, I choose salvage: none.

I will update this playbook after each patrol based on observed alliance patterns, escort reciprocity, and hit/miss statistics, preserving what worked and discarding predictable behaviors that opponents exploited.

1.text:
When I must pick a hide cell, I vary between off-center and center to avoid predictability, but I will repeat a successful/defensive center hide when I am protecting a lead or want balanced coverage; do not repeat the same non-central cell twice in a row unless a clear strategic reason exists.

When the standing order tells me which station to fire at, I follow the standing order unless the target is Harbor and I am willing to accept being jettisoned; otherwise do not fire on Harbor.

When I choose a firing coordinate, prefer center or near-center for balanced coverage and higher hit probability, but alternate with offset cells across rounds to retain unpredictability unless preserving a lead or maintaining pressure warrants repeating center.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I publicly claim exactly that result — claims must match the office report.

When composing station notes, mirror cooperative language of presumed allies to avoid standing out and to probe reciprocity; explicitly state that I am watching nominations/votes and will flag deviations. Avoid accusations unless I have decisive information.

When other boats show coordinated messaging, mirror that coordination until I see evidence of betrayal; use mirroring to probe alignment through reactions to nominations/votes and to invite explicit reciprocal commitments.

When an escort payoff is only possible if two boats name each other, claim an escort only if I reasonably expect reciprocity — e.g., prior explicit mutual signals, recent reciprocal behavior, or a direct promise — otherwise claim none. If mutual confirmations are explicit and contemporaneous (both name each other in notes or signals that round), go ahead and claim escort to capture the 5-point mutual payoff.

When my score is substantially positive relative to others, avoid risky plays (e.g., attacking Harbor, needless exposure) and favor conservative hiding, consistent firing choices that protect the lead, truthful claims, and measured communication to avoid provoking coordinated retaliation.

When my shot hits a rival and that yields a useful score swing, continue pressure on that station per standing order to maintain advantage; when it misses, acknowledge it truthfully and resume probing via notes and vote monitoring.

When considering attacking Harbor for the payroll, weigh immediate +3 vs guarantee of being targeted by Harbor’s deterrent; do not attack Harbor unless the strategic value of forcing Harbor off outweighs losing my ability to continue the patrol.

When votes/nominations are presented, record and publicly reference anomalies and deviations in my notes to help identify coordination or betrayal among others; use those public references to justify future escort claims or targeting choices.

Do not attempt to falsely report shot results; instead use hide choices, firing-cell variation, note-mirroring, and selective escort claims as my levers.

New refinements from recent rounds:
- If I have repeatedly scored hits on a particular opponent and public claims corroborate that pattern, continue focusing fire per standing order while using notes to encourage allies to reciprocate escorts/payoffs.
- If two allies have been signaling mutual escort over multiple rounds but do not explicitly mutual-name in the escort stage, continue mirroring their notes but only claim escort when I have explicit reciprocal commitment or when the payoff is likely that round.
- If the group’s public messaging converges (three-way mutual confirmations), I can be more aggressive with claiming escorts and conserving central hides because the group stability lowers the chance of sudden betrayal.
- If the picket shows signs of fragile coordination (conflicting public signals about who is allied), prioritize conservative play: truthful claims, no risky Harbor shots, fewer escort claims, and hides chosen to minimize exposure.

I will revise tactics in future games by keeping these rules and these new conditional refinements: mirror to probe, claim escort only with high likelihood of reciprocity, repeat center when protecting a lead, always tell the office result truthfully, and avoid Harbor unless the payoff justifies removal.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that avoids obvious patterns: vary between edges and interior, avoid repeating the same number twice in a row, and prefer cells away from where I see others consistently firing. If a specific opponent is repeatedly hitting my station, bias hides away from the cells they most often fire.

When given the standing firing order, follow it unless there is a clear, deliberate reason to break it; do not randomly override the standing order. If a deliberate break is considered (to retaliate or remove Harbor), be prepared for reputational and point consequences and only do so with a clear plan.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report that result honestly in the public claim (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss). Consistent honesty preserves credibility for escort negotiations.

When posting a station note, mirror the tone and basic content of cooperative players to signal alignment, then add one short line that probes for deviation (e.g., “I’ll mirror key voters; flag any deviations”) rather than inventing complex narratives. Keep notes short, concrete, and consistent with prior posts.

When I want escort points, name only actual fleet boat names. Only claim to have escorted a specific boat if I expect a reciprocal claim or if I can plausibly induce reciprocity via notes and past credibility; otherwise claim none. If I name a partner, explicitly request reciprocation in the note and only follow through on the salvage claim if reciprocation is likely.

When two-way escort reciprocity is plausible, pursue it: use notes to explicitly suggest mutual escort and follow through to get the 5-point exchanges. Prefer forming mutual escorts with players who have been cooperative and have credible public claims; avoid offering escorts to players who have repeatedly shot and hit me.

Do not fire on Harbor except as an explicit, premeditated strategy to remove Harbor; recognize this forces jettison and transfers 3 points and will be noticed. Treat Harbor as a protected/expensive target by default.

When choosing firing coordinates, balance unpredictability with hit probability: avoid always choosing the same “safe” number; bias shots toward center cells when trying to maximize hit chance but mix in off-center shots to avoid being predictable. If an opponent’s hide-pattern is apparent, target the cells they favor when the standing order directs me to fire at them.

When my shot hits, use that public hit claim to build credibility for later reciprocal escort negotiations; when my shot misses, accept the credibility hit and use notes to restore alignment with allies or to justify strategic shifts.

When others’ notes and nominations are consistent and cooperative, continue mirroring to maintain coalition and probe; when someone deviates in wording or voting, call out the deviation succinctly and adjust my mirror stance accordingly. If a supposed ally begins attacking me, downgrade them from potential escort partner and stop mirroring.

Do not name non-existent boats or out-of-scope labels in salvage/escort claims—this is invalid and ineffective.

When no clear escort partner exists and reciprocity is unlikely, claim none rather than making a random claim that offers no benefit.

When the round sequence shows someone consistently hitting me or another ally, prioritize hiding pattern changes and coordinate via notes to either avoid their targeting pattern or to set up reciprocal escorts that offset losses. If the aggressor is in the standing firing order before me (i.e., will fire at me in sequence), consider hiding shifts that exploit their observed firing bias.

When making any public message, keep it short, actionable, and consistent with my past claims to preserve credibility.

Additions based on play experience:
- Avoid repeating the same hide number in consecutive rounds; doing so made me more predictable and was exploited. Track my last two hides and vary the next pick.
- If a player (e.g., Foxtrot) repeatedly scores hits on me, treat them as untrustworthy for escort purposes and prioritize forming or maintaining escorts with other cooperative players (e.g., Echo) instead of them.
- If coalition partners publicly pledge mutual escorts but fail to reciprocate in salvage, call it out concisely in notes and stop committing to that partner until reciprocity is restored.
- Use successful hits and earned credibility to lock in escort agreements in the closing rounds; when behind on points late in the patrol, be more willing to push for guaranteed escort exchanges rather than gamble on uncertain hits.
- Track public firing and hit/miss patterns of each opponent across rounds; use that small pattern dataset to choose hides and to select likely-hit firing cells when I have the shot at them.

I will follow this playbook in future patrols and apply the adjustments above in real time.
